a.name: Thunder cleave
a.desc: A huge low crash with a rolling thunder tail, heavy and dark.
a.note: kl-ex1dd heavy impact (body, peak in first 35 ms) + sword impact for a steel bite on the front + huge explosion thunder low-passed as the tail.

b.name: Temple gong blast
b.desc: A great old gong struck hard, ringing out with a faint magic shimmer.
b.note: low gong bash (Freesound) as body + bright trailer clang for the strike + glimmer ring tail, quiet, for the mystical side.

c.name: Steel strike blast
c.desc: A giant blade strike that bursts into a wide explosion.
c.note: metal hit 2 (dense steel strike, crest 6 dB, rise 15 ms) + deep boom high-passed for weight + Supernatural Explosion (Freesound) under it as the burst.

a.name: War drum roll
a.desc: A rolling war drum swells up and lands on a deep boom.
a.note: timpani riser cut to its last crescendo (about 550 ms) + deep hit landing on its top; drum roll tail keeps going under.

b.name: Glass bell swell
b.desc: A glassy ringing swell rises and opens into soft old chimes.
b.note: reversed champagne-flute ring (glassy, tonal) cut to its last ~560 ms + wind chimes on its peak, magic but old.

c.name: Blades drawn
c.desc: A rising metal ring that ends as swords slide out of their sheaths.
c.note: reversed metal pole hit pitched down 3 (a rising steel ring) + sword unsheath (Freesound) on its peak + small metal hit ringing out after, like blades held high.

a.name: Dark drum hit
a.desc: One low, dark drum hit with an iron edge, short and ominous.
a.note: dark orchestral timpani (rise 11 ms, low) + metal screen-door slam for an iron edge so it cuts through.

b.name: Blade scrape
b.desc: A sharp metal clang that grinds into a short iron scrape.
b.note: long metal scrape (Freesound) from its clang at 250 ms + heavy metal thud on ground under it for weight.

c.name: Warning bell
c.desc: A deep iron bell struck once, like an alarm in the dark.
c.note: Kenney heavy bell pitched down 5 for a deep iron toll + close thump quiet for a dull front; cut to 560 ms with a 260 ms fade so it never drones.

a.name: Heavy air rush
a.desc: A low, heavy whoosh of a big body rushing at you.
a.note: short low whoosh pitched down 2, cut to start in its quiet lead-in so it swells to a peak near 125 ms.

b.name: Fast sharp swish
b.desc: A quick, bright swish, like something thin and fast darting in.
b.note: fast swish transition from its quiet start (peak near 120 ms) + Kenney cloth flap quiet for a body.

c.name: Rags and rush
c.desc: Ragged cloth flaps as a body rushes forward, with a foot scuff.
c.note: Kenney cloth flap (from 40 ms, the flap) + mid whoosh for the body rush peaking near 120 ms + quiet grass footstep as the push-off scuff.

a.name: Stone crack quake
a.desc: Rock smashes into stone ground and gravel scatters around.
a.note: rock impact (Freesound) for the crack + heavy wheelbarrow dropped on concrete for a rattling stone body + gravel impacts low-passed as scattering debris.

layers.credit: "Gravel Impacts and Falls.wav" by lolamadeus, CC0, https://freesound.org/people/lolamadeus/sounds/179341

b.name: Timber crash
b.desc: A huge wooden crash on the forest floor, hollow and booming.
b.note: old heavy wooden door kicked (fast, dense wood hit) + tree trunk ground impact + body falls on wood for a hollow boom.

c.name: Muddy thud
c.desc: A heavy body thuds into wet mud, then a deep rumble rolls out.
c.note: close thump + Kenney heavy punch for a meaty body + wet splat (Freesound) on top for the bog.

a.name: Dark metal swell
a.desc: A grim metallic hum that swells and snaps off at the hit.
a.note: metallic horror riser from 520 ms (its last ~0.9 s), pitched down 2 for weight + backwards whoosh low layer peaking at the same end; loudest at 89% of the length.

b.name: Reverse cymbal
b.desc: A cymbal crash played backwards, rising fast into the strike.
b.note: reversed cymbal hits from 300 ms (quiet start), a clean classic swell whose loudest point is its very end (97%).

c.name: Wet inhale
c.desc: A wet, rotten slurp of breath sucked in before the hit.
c.note: inhale with glass leads as a quiet breath swell, coffee slurp (reversed wet suck-in) joins at 150 ms; both peak near the end.
